summary: The note profiles Ms. Clara Bennett, a middle school math teacher in Millford who used big data analytics to personalize instruction and turn around struggling students during the 2023-2024 school year. Using platforms like LearnSphere and EdInsight, she tailored homework, challenges and feedback, then spread the approach across subjects through data-sharing and monthly 'Data Days'. The piece argues that data analytics, paired with a teacher's care, improves test scores, engagement and self-esteem.
one_line: Middle school teacher Clara Bennett uses big data analytics tools to personalize learning, boost outcomes and spark cross-curricular collaboration in Millford schools.
key_facts: Clara Bennett is a middle school mathematics teacher in the suburban Millford school district with 10 years of teaching experience.
On September 5, 2023, as the school year began, Clara Bennett decided to change her approach and started a deep dive into big data analytics.
Clara Bennett learned analytics through online courses, professional development workshops and educational technology blogs, and calls herself a 'data advocate'.
Clara began using the platforms LearnSphere and EdInsight in mid-October 2023 for diagnostic assessments and tracking skill progression.
By November 2023, each student in Clara's class had a learning journey mapped out using her analytics tools.
By December 2023, Clara had fine-tuned her curriculum so each student received individualized homework, targeted in-class challenges and personalized feedback based on data profiles.
Results included improved test scores, increased engagement and a boost in students' self-esteem.
Clara adopted monthly 'Data Days' on January 15, 2024, where students review progress charts and set goals together.
By February 2024, other Millford School District teachers became interested, and Clara started a cross-curricular data-sharing collaboration.
An example of cross-curricular sharing: a student's strength in understanding graphs in math could help a history teacher teach historical trends.
Clara faced obstacles including software selection, choosing data visualization techniques and initial student resistance to the 'clinical' approach.
By Spring 2024, students once deemed at risk of falling behind were mastering new challenges.
